Carla M: Quick Q — following the attribution RFC follow-up: can we use session-sticky routing for short-lived streaming requests so the same inference pool keeps the KV/cache and our attribution stays stable?

Dmitri K: Short answer: yes, but tradeoffs. Sticky gives better cache locality => lower tail latency and fewer cold KV fetches. Downside: skew and harder failover across AZs, and reprocessing/backfills need canonical keys to reconcile.

Alice S: Ops concern: if we do sticky, ensure every event still contains a canonical attribution fingerprint so audits/backfills can reassign if session moved. Also need offsets and append-only canonical log for replay.

Bob L: Also cost/throughput angle: sticky can cause hot partitions (some tenants bursty). We should bound sticky TTL and have a de-sticky policy when partition CPU or queue length > threshold.

Dmitri K: Proposed design sketch:
- Router chooses between: deterministic shard (tenant_id hash) OR sticky lease (session_id -> chosen-worker)
- Sticky lease TTL e.g. 30s, renewable on activity, evict when load high
- Events always carry canonical fields for later reconciliation (fingerprint, canonical_attrib_id, original_session_id)

Example event we’d emit (included in every path):
```json
{
  "tenant_id":"acct_123",
  "session_id":"s-abc123",
  "canonical_attrib":"fp:v2:sha256:0a1b2c",
  "seq":102,
  "ingest_ts":"2026-03-22T16:12:03Z",
  "payload_tokens":45
}
```

Carla M: That canonical id is critical. If we reprocess after a shard move we can stitch events by canonical_attrib and rebuild billing with deterministic joins.

Alice S: Late-arrival policy: keep a 24h late-arrival window for full reconciliation, after which audits produce a "late-adjustment" event and attach a reason code. Need tooling in console to surface these adjustments per-tenant.

Bob L: On skew mitigation: implement a sticky-capacity check in router: if worker.load > 0.75 or sticky_count>max_sticky_per_worker then refuse lease and fall back to tenant hash routing. Emit metric sticky_lease_rejected{tenant}.

Dmitri K: For cross-dc failover: sticky leases should be local-only. Add a fallback rewrite marker when a request is served by a different worker: canonical_attrib remains same, add header fallback_origin and fallback_reason (e.g., "zone-failover", "evicted"). That way downstream audits know it was a fallback, not a duplicate.

Carla M: Rollout plan idea: default routing = deterministic tenant hash. Enable sticky behind a feature-flag per-tenant for high-QPS customers for 2-week canary. Collect latency_p95, cache_hit_ratio, sticky_evictions, late_adjustments.

Dmitri K: Implementation checklist:
- router: sticky lease table (TTL, renew, eviction)
- event contract: canonical_attrib + fallback metadata + ingest_ts + seq
- storage: append-only canonical store + offset checkpoints for replay
- console: adjustments UI + per-tenant sticky metrics

Carla M: Decision summary: go hybrid. No global sticky by default. Sticky enabled per-tenant with bounded TTL and eviction. Always emit canonical attribution for auditability. 24h reconcile window and explicit late-adjust events. Canary rollout + dashboards before flip. :thumbsup:

Alice S: SGTM. Will add runbook entries for sticky eviction incidents and reconciliation playbook.

Bob L: I'll prototype the router lease algorithm this week and post perf numbers.

infra-bot: Deploy scheduled: feature-flag "sticky-routing" will be available in canary next Tue.
